proposedchanges.title: Trump Officials Add Journalist to Signal Group on Houthi Policy Coordination
proposedchanges.description_long: National Security Adviser Michael Waltz created a Signal group called “Houthi PC small group” in March 2025 to coordinate policy and operations involving Yemen’s Houthis. He added Atlantic editor Jeffrey Goldberg, who was not an intended participant. Messages in the group discussed the coming 72 hours, and Waltz asked officials to identify staff contacts for follow-up coordination. The group included senior administration officials. Goldberg later described receiving the messages, bringing attention to the group’s purpose and membership. His inclusion exposed internal deliberations to a journalist. The disclosure raised questions about the handling of sensitive national-security planning and officials’ communications practices. The supplied account does not establish that the chat changed the military operation or affected its outcome.

evidencebasis: The packet and merged descriptions identify Waltz’s Signal group, Goldberg’s unintended inclusion, its Houthi coordination subject, and the coming 72-hour period. The long ends mid-sentence and refers to a separate strike-plan record. The source URL remains present.
notes: The medium is concise and distinct from the longer account. Complete the cut-off long, remove cross-entry commentary, and keep the topic limited to the group documented here.

proposedchanges.title: DHS Testimony Describes Tiger Team Reports on Student Protesters
proposedchanges.description_long: In July court testimony, senior Department of Homeland Security official Peter Hatch described analysts forming a “Tiger Team” to review student protesters. The summarized testimony says the team used names from Canary Mission and another list and prepared reports on more than 5,000 people. Homeland Security Investigations sent information to the State Department for possible removal decisions. Hatch reportedly said he had verbal direction to consult Canary Mission, though he did not regard it as authoritative. The summary says the discussion included phrases such as “free Palestine.” The account describes information used in immigration review; it does not establish that every person listed faced enforcement or was removed, or that either list determined a case.

proposedchanges.title: Shoshana Chatfield Removed as U.S. Representative to NATO Military Committee
proposedchanges.description_long: Vice Admiral Shoshana Chatfield’s removal ended her service as the U.S. representative to NATO’s Military Committee. The decision was announced on April 7, 2025, without a public explanation, and Brigadier General Sean Flynn was named to serve in an acting capacity. European officials expressed concern about the signal the change might send for U.S. security commitments, but the personnel move did not itself announce a change in NATO policy. Right-wing advocacy groups had criticized Chatfield over diversity initiatives, and observers questioned whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was involved. No public evidence confirmed that Hegseth ordered her removal or established who initiated it. The reason for the decision remained unknown.

evidencebasis: The packet and merged descriptions identify Chatfield’s April 7, 2025 removal, the lack of a public reason, Flynn’s acting role, and the absence of confirmed evidence that Hegseth ordered it. The source URL remains present.
notes: Keep the uncertainty about who initiated the removal. Replace the title’s asserted motive and complete the cut-off long; remove unrelated Iran-war tags.
